title: Opening the topics wiped a level check left part way
body:
## Summary
The menu's "My topics" (plan-open) and "New topics" (plan-propose) replaced a level check left part way with a blank plan check, losing the learner's answers while home promised "Your place is saved".

## Description
A check and its topic plan share one session slot (s.check). checkCommand built the plan check from `open` only when it stood at verdict or plan, else from `blank(...)` (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:365), so an open check in its about or tasks stage was overwritten. Home draws such a check as "check-part-way" with "Your place is saved" (desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:466-469), and the menu offers "My topics" on every Linga screen (desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:754). Fixed: plan-open and plan-propose now refuse (409) while the open check is in about or tasks (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:363-364); Carry on and Start again are unchanged.

## Flow
- learner with a placement and a plan starts "Find my level again", answers one question, leaves
- menu -> My topics -> plan-open -> checkCommand -> blank(learnerId, "plan") replaces the open check
- observed: s.check is a new id at stage plan with 0 turns; the part-way answers are gone
- fix: refuse plan-open/plan-propose while open.stage is about or tasks; new suite tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs pins it

## Expected impact
A learner mid re-check who opens their topics keeps their place instead of silently losing up to seven minutes of answers. Could break: a flow that relied on topics replacing a part-way check now gets a refusal line (the menu still offers the door; see the ux-reviewer card).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a part-way level check survives opening the topics
Before: probe through englishCommand (stub engine): 1 of 3 answers given, left, then plan-open -> stage plan, 0 turns, a new check id (lost); same for plan-propose
After: refused 409 "Your level check is part way...", same check id, stage about, 3 turns kept; re-measured on the commit
Method: gate - tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs case 1, red on HEAD ("Missing expected rejection: plan-open"), green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:365 `const base = open && (open.stage === "verdict" || open.stage === "plan") ? open : blank(learnerId, "plan");`
desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:469 home "check-part-way": "Your place is saved"
desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:754 menu act("my-topics", ... cmd(l.plan ? "plan-open" : "plan-propose"))
probe output before: `before: stage about turns 3` -> `after plan-open: stage plan turns 0 same check false`

title: A judge misquote made the learner resend a valid level-check answer
body:
## Summary
When the level-check judge's quote was not an exact excerpt of the answer, check.ts threw at once and the phone told the learner to send the answer again; it is now re-asked once inside the same call.

## Description
The judge's quote admits the verdict, so it must be an exact substring of the response (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:448). A miss threw "The judge did not quote the learner accurately." and the call's failure line asked the learner to resend. The LT runs recorded it three times (uat/runs/2026-10-14-lt/oksana-34.md:35, uat/runs/2026-10-14-lt/recert-6/martin-45.md:35, uat/runs/2026-10-17-lt-swap-2/recert-1/martin-45.json), with the acceptance "retried inside the app, the learner is never asked to resend". The task and plan calls in the same file already re-ask once with the miss named (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:185-205, 311-321); the judge did not. Fixed per the registry's structured-output golden path (repair is a bounded loop) and technique graded-span-grounding (only an exact span admits): one re-ask naming the miss, booked as the next try (types.ts Again); the exact check stays and a second miss is refused as before.

## Flow
- learner answers a say task; the judge returns a quote that is not in the response
- before: throw -> call() commits "Linga could not read that answer... send it again" -> the learner retypes
- after: grounded() fails -> console.info + one re-ask with the quote named -> grounded -> task judged; twice wrong -> refused as before

## Expected impact
Fewer level-check answers bounced back to the learner; one extra judge call only on a miss. Could break: a judge that misquotes systematically now costs two calls before the same refusal.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a misquoted judge reading is repaired inside the call
Before: stub judge misquoting once: learner resends 1, judge calls 1, check.error set ("send it again")
After: learner resends 0, judge calls 2, task judged with the learner's exact excerpt; misquoting twice: refused, judge calls 2 (one re-ask, never more)
Method: gate - tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs case 2 against the stubbed text engine, red on the parent commit, green after; the live rate of misquotes was not measurable without a live run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts (before) `if (... || !quote || !response.includes(quote)) throw new Error("The judge did not quote the learner accurately.");`
uat/runs/2026-10-14-lt/recert-6/report.md:225-229 LT-martin-45-J1-3 "Judge quote check rejected a valid answer"; acceptance "Quote validation is retried inside the app"
uat/runs/2026-10-14-lt/oksana-34.md:35 "Judge quote failure forced a retype"

title: Refused level-check commands named a task or question that was not there
body:
## Summary
checkRefusal told the phone "Carry on with the tasks" after the tasks were done, "Answer the one on the TV" with no task on the TV, and "Linga already knows what to plan for" before any plan: 17 of 75 refusals misdirected.

## Description
checkRefusal (desk/src/lib/english/activity.ts:95-105) is the sentence the phone shows for a 409 from CHECK_ACCEPTS. check-answer outside about fell through to "The questions are done. Carry on with the tasks." in verdict and plan states; check-task fell through to BY_ACTION's "This task has changed. Answer the one on the TV." in the about, verdict and plan states; plan-goal before the plan stage got "Linga already knows what to plan for." Each names a cause that is not this one. Fixed: those three say where the check is ("The level check is done. Carry on from the TV.", "Answer Linga's questions first.", "Find your level before choosing topics.").

## Flow
- a late or duplicate phone post (e.g. a reply sent after the verdict) reaches checkCommand
- checkAccepts refuses -> checkRefusal picks the sentence
- before: the learner is sent to tasks or a TV task that do not exist; after: told the check is done or what comes first

## Expected impact
A learner whose post is refused reads where the check stands instead of a wrong instruction. Could break: nothing pins the old strings (git grep found no other consumer).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every refusal names the stage the check is in
Before: 17 misdirecting refusals of 75 (10 idle states x 12 commands): check-answer 4, check-task 6, plan-goal 7
After: 0 of 75
Method: gate - tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs case 3 walks every idle state and command; red on the parent (21 flagged lines), green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/activity.ts:98 (before) `if (action === "check-answer") return k.stage === "about" ? "Linga has not asked a question yet." : "The questions are done. Carry on with the tasks.";`
desk/src/lib/english/activity.ts:89 BY_ACTION["check-task"] = "This task has changed. Answer the one on the TV."
desk/src/lib/english/activity.ts:90 BY_ACTION["plan-goal"] = "Linga already knows what to plan for."

title: Two headers said a high read needs two strong passes; the rule is three
body:
## Summary
cert.ts's issuing rule 1 and staircase's summary stated that high confidence rests on two strong passes; HIGH_STRONG_PASSES is 3 since the 2026-10-14 recerts.

## Description
HIGH_STRONG_PASSES = 3 (desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:153, raised after six of eight high placements were one band high). cert.ts:8 still read "HIGH confidence (placement.ts staircase: two strong passes under a real ceiling)", in the header a teacher is asked to read before the certificate is promised, and placement.ts:162 read "Confidence is high only with two strong passes at the band". Both now name the constant.

## Flow
- read cert.ts rule 1 or staircase's summary
- before: told two strong passes certify; code demands three
- after: both name HIGH_STRONG_PASSES; a test pins it

## Expected impact
A teacher or builder reading the certification rule reads the rule the code runs. Comment-only; nothing can break.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated certification rule matches the code
Before: 2 stale statements of the high rule (git grep -n -i "two strong" desk/src)
After: 0; tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs case 4 fails on either phrase
Method: gate - source test, red on the parent commit ("placement.ts states the old rule"), green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:153 `export const HIGH_STRONG_PASSES = 3;`
desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:8 (before) "HIGH confidence (placement.ts staircase: two strong passes under a real ceiling)"
desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:162 (before) "Confidence is high only with two strong passes at the band"

title: The Cambridge coverage report carried its own TypeScript loader
body:
## Summary
tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs hand-copied the require hook (no cache, no .tsx) instead of tools/ts-load.cjs, the rules suites' one loader.

## Description
Ten tools in tools/ copy the TypeScript require hook by hand; ts-load.cjs is the shared one with a disk cache of transpiles and .tsx support. The report (tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs:6-11) transpiled every module on every run. It now requires ts-load.cjs (one line).

## Flow
- node tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs
- before: 6 loader lines, fresh transpile each run
- after: require('./ts-load.cjs'), cached transpiles; output byte-identical

## Expected impact
The report runs about five times faster and follows the loader the suites use. Could break: nothing; output diffed identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - report wall time
Before: 424-511 ms over 3 runs
After: 82-167 ms over 5 runs (167 ms while the cache filled); output identical (diff exit 0)
Method: probe - timed the same command on both sides on this tree; no gate runs the report
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs:6-11 (before) Module._resolveFilename override + require.extensions[".ts"] = ... ts.transpileModule(...)
`git grep -l "require.extensions\['.ts'\]" -- tools` -> 10 hand copies besides ts-load.cjs

title: The Cambridge claim floor can never bind: coverage is 100% at every age
body:
## Summary
claimAllowed() needs VERIFIED and A2 Key coverage >= 90%, but coverage counts a descriptor as practised when any authored scene has one of its skills, so the share is 1.0 for every age 0-99 and the floor is decoration.

## Description
coverage() (desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:109-115) marks a descriptor practised when some allowed scene's skill is in the descriptor's skills list. Each of the eight skills has an authored scene at every age, so all 16 A2 and 23 B1 descriptors read "yes" (tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs prints e.g. "Describe a photograph alone for about a minute [describe] weekend"). The plan's kill criterion (CLAIM_FLOOR = 0.9, desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:119-121) therefore rests on VERIFIED alone; a person flipping VERIFIED turns the Cambridge wording on with no coverage test that could fail. The suite pins coverage numbers derived from the same table (tools/cambridge-rules-test.cjs:54-66), the hand-list-reads-itself shape of §4.7. Fixed would mean a descriptor counts only by a scene that names it (e.g. a `descriptors` field on scenes, or the practice part mapping), so the share can fall below the floor.

## Flow
- for age in 0..99, exam in both: coverage(exam, age).share
- observed: min share 1 (probe)
- consequence: claimAllowed() === VERIFIED for every age

## Expected impact
Before any "A2 Key" claim reaches a screen, the 90% floor would mean something. Could break: tightening the mapping may drop coverage well below 90% and keep the claim off, which is the floor working.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the claim gate has a test that can fail
Before: min coverage share over ages 0-99 and both papers: 1.0 (probe script over coverage())
After: not measurable until a person decides what counts as practising a descriptor; the instrument is the same probe over the new mapping
Method: probe for Before; After needs the teacher's mapping, so the ladder stops at a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
probe: `for age 0..99 for exam of EXAMS: min(coverage(exam,age).share)` -> 1
desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:113 `scenesFor[d.id] = scenes.filter((x) => d.skills.includes(x.skill))`
desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:121 `return VERIFIED && coverage("a2-key-schools", age).share >= CLAIM_FLOOR;`
escalation: direction - what "practised" means for a descriptor is a teacher's call (cambridge.ts asks a teacher to read the table)

title: LG-54's verdict reason and the judge's heldBack reach no screen since TL-12
body:
## Summary
verdictReason (placement.ts) and the judge's heldBack excerpt were built for LG-54 to keep a "fail" from sitting beside praise; their only consumer, the phone's "What Linga saw", was removed by TL-12, so the judge still writes heldBack on every call and nothing shows it.

## Description
verdictReason (desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:110-125) has no consumer in desk/src: `git grep -n verdictReason -- desk/src` lists only its definition; tools/linga-rules-test.cjs tests it. Commit b65d7d77 (TL-12, "the TV drives, the phone speaks") removed the LingaPhone `<details>What Linga saw</details>` block that called it. The judge prompt still asks for heldBack (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:443), keepHeldBack stores it (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:462), cleanTask keeps it on disk (desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:324), and only verdictReason reads it. docs/BACKLOG.md:389 still says "the phone's What Linga saw shows it". LG-54's promise (the learner sees why a task did not pass) holds on no surface.

## Flow
- learner fails a level-check task below its band
- judge returns heldBack; code stores it beside the verdict
- no screen renders verdictReason or the task list; the reason exists only on disk

## Expected impact
Either the learner sees why a task did not pass again (LG-54), or the judge stops producing a field nothing reads (a shorter judge answer per task, one less stored field). Could break: dropping heldBack changes the judge prompt (a live drift record).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a built rule reaches the learner, or stops costing
Before: consumers of verdictReason in desk/src: 0; judge fields produced and never shown per judged task: 1 (heldBack)
After: not measurable until the owner picks show or drop; either side has a gate (a TV view test, or a zero-reference grep)
Method: probe (zero-consumer grep) for Before; the After is a product choice
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: `git grep -n verdictReason -- desk/src` -> desk/src/lib/english/placement.ts:110 only `git show b65d7d77 | grep verdictReason` -> the removed LingaPhone import and `{verdictReason(t)&&{verdictReason(t)}}` desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:443 heldBack instruction; desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:462 keepHeldBack docs/BACKLOG.md:389 "the phone's \"What Linga saw\" shows it"
escalation: direction - show the task reasons on the TV (On Air: a picture, prose only in the caption) or drop verdictReason and the heldBack field

title: The certificate plate prints topic-title digits despite its no-digit rule
body:
## Summary
cert.ts promises the plate carries no digit but the band's and steers its quote away from digits, but copies plan topic titles verbatim, and a model-written title like "Top 5 games" prints its digit on the plate and in certWords.

## Description
The header (desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:25-26) and monthOf (desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:238) hold the plate to "no digit but the band's"; evidenceFor prefers a quote without a digit (desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:109-114). Topics are copied as titled (desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:137, 263, 276), and cleanTopic accepts digits in a title (probe: cleanTopic keeps "Planning a 3-day school trip"). The cert suite's fixtures spell ordinals ("My first topic", tools/cert-rules-test.cjs:178) so its no-digit asserts (cert 13, cert 15) never meet a digit title. One rule, two implementations: the quote obeys it, the topics do not.

## Flow
- plan topic titled "Top 5 games" is agreed, the certificate issues
- plateOf/certWords copy the title
- observed: "Your topics: Planning a 3-day school trip, Top 5 games." - 2 digits beyond the band

## Expected impact
The plate keeps the promise it states, or the promise is narrowed honestly. Could break: dropping a digit-titled topic hides a topic the learner chose.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the plate obeys its own no-digit rule
Before: probe: certWords of a cert with 2 digit titles -> 2 digits beyond the band
After: not measurable until the rule is chosen; the gate is cert 13/15 with a digit-titled fixture
Method: probe for Before; After waits on a product rule
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
probe output: `Your topics: Planning a 3-day school trip, Top 5 games.` / `digits beyond band: 2`
desk/src/lib/english/cert.ts:137 `const topics = (l.plan?.topics ?? []).map(t => t.title.trim().slice(0, TITLE_MAX))`
tools/cert-rules-test.cjs:178 fixture titles "My first topic", "My second topic"
escalation: direction - which rule bends: leave a digit-titled topic off the plate, spell it, or narrow the "no digit" promise to counts

title: The goal task puts learner-derived goal text in the instruction, not the data
body:
## Summary
goalTask(aim) interpolates the aim of the learner's goal into the task instruction string; the plan path passes the learner's own words as a data field (learnerAsked) instead.

## Description
The aim comes from k.goal, which the about step's model extracted from what the learner said (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:399), and goalTask writes it inside quotes into `task` (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:71, 180), the field the model reads as instructions; the re-ask does the same (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:201). checkSystem tells the model only the learner's input JSON is untrusted. planAsk, the sibling, keeps the learner's words in `learnerAsked` and refers to it by name (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:265-266). Registry prompt-safety/untrusted-span-fencing: data carries a provenance label and stays out of the instruction channel. Fixed: put the aim in request.learner.goalAim and say "set this task in learner.goalAim".

## Flow
- learner states a goal in the about questions; the about model returns goal
- advance -> goalTaskDue -> goalTask(aim) -> request.task contains the aim verbatim
- fix: move the aim to a data field, reference it by name, as learnerAsked does

## Expected impact
Learner text stops reaching the instruction channel of the task call; the goal-task behaviour (LG-55) must hold. Could break: the model may set fewer tasks in the goal when the aim is referenced rather than quoted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - learner-derived text stays in the data channel
Before: learner-derived strings interpolated into an instruction field in check.ts: 2 sites (goalTask, the goal re-ask)
After: predicted 0, with learnerAsked as the pattern; not measured: the behaviour half needs a live run
Method: simulation - walked the LG-55 path and the plan path; the stub gate is S but the goal-task rate needs a live LT run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:71 `export const goalTask = (aim: string) => `The learner stated a goal ... "${aim}". Set this task in that aim...``
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:180 `task: `Write one ${kind} task ...${goalDue ? ` ${goalTask(aim)}` : ""}``
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:265 `...(asked ? { learnerAsked: asked } : {})`
instrument: a stub-engine case in tools/linga-level-rules-test.cjs capturing the task request: no learner-derived string (goal aim, twin prompt) inside request.task, the aim present as a data field (learner.goalAim); then one live LT recert of the LG-55 goal-task branch (operator) to show the goal-task rate holds

title: The placement sim's child has no desk/data refusal its two sibling tools have
body:
## Summary
linga-school-live.cjs and linga-cert-live.cjs refuse a DESK_DATA_DIR inside desk/data; linga-placement-sim.cjs's child, which resets the session and saves placements for learners "ema" and "jakub", checks nothing.

## Description
The parent sets DESK_DATA_DIR per persona (tools/linga-placement-sim.cjs:37), but the child path runs on SIM_PERSONA alone (tools/linga-placement-sim.cjs:27, 49): run with SIM_PERSONA set and no DESK_DATA_DIR, it writes the real learners' records under desk/data (repo law: never touch desk/data) and spends live calls. The siblings refuse at their top (tools/linga-school-live.cjs:17-19, tools/linga-cert-live.cjs:24-26). One rule, three tools, two implement it.

## Flow
- SIM_PERSONA=young-a1 node tools/linga-placement-sim.cjs (no DESK_DATA_DIR)
- child -> dispatch reset, learner.set ema -> check-start ... saveEnglish(ema)
- fix: the same three-line refusal as the siblings, at the top of child()

## Expected impact
A mistyped invocation can no longer overwrite Ema's or Jakub's level record. Could break: nothing; the parent always sets a scratch dir.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every live tool in this context refuses desk/data
Before: tools with the desk/data refusal: 2 of 3
After: predicted 3 of 3
Method: simulation - the Before cannot be run without writing desk/data and spending model calls; read from the source
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
tools/linga-school-live.cjs:19 `if (data === real || data.startsWith(real + path.sep)) throw new Error('Refusing to run against desk/data...')`
tools/linga-cert-live.cjs:26 (same)
tools/linga-placement-sim.cjs:27 `if (process.env.SIM_PERSONA) child(process.env.SIM_PERSONA)` - no DESK_DATA_DIR check in child()
instrument: a spawn test: SIM_PERSONA=young-a1 with DESK_DATA_DIR unset (and set to desk/data) must exit non-zero before any require of the store or the engine; seeded red cannot be taken on HEAD without writing desk/data, so the worker runs the After only and takes the Before by reading

title: Two live Linga tools still hand-copy the TypeScript loader
body:
## Summary
tools/linga-cert-live.cjs:30-34 and tools/linga-placement-sim.cjs:51-54 copy the require hook that tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs dropped in da554136.

## Description
Same copy as the built cambridge-coverage finding: no transpile cache, no .tsx hook, a third spelling of the "@/" alias. Not built this round because neither tool can be run in a sweep (one needs a dev server, the other spends model calls), so the change has no gate here.

## Flow
- replace the copied loader with `const { root } = require('./ts-load.cjs')`
- node --check both
- dry-load their module lists through the instrument

## Expected impact
One loader for every tool that loads desk TypeScript in this context. Could break: a tool that relied on the hand copy's exact options.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - loader copies in this context
Before: 2 hand copies left in linga-level's tools (3 before da554136)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - the tools cannot run offline in a sweep; the instrument above is the gate
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a dry load of each tool's TS modules with no server and no engine (LINGA_CERT_URL unset skips linga-cert-live before its loader; a harness that requires the tool's module list through ts-load.cjs and diffs the exports)

title: The menu still offers "My topics" while a level check is part way
body:
## Summary
Since 4ca4495f the server refuses plan-open/plan-propose while a check is part way, but the menu (view.ts) still offers "My topics", so the learner presses it and gets a refusal line.

## Description
The guard lives in check.ts (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:363-364); the menu builds act("my-topics", ...) unconditionally (desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:754). activity.ts's own rule is that the view disables what the table refuses ("the view disables the same actions", desk/src/lib/english/activity.ts:10-12). view.ts belongs to the linga context, so this round did not edit it (veto 1).

## Flow
- part-way check, open the Linga menu
- press My topics -> 409 "Your level check is part way..."
- fix: disable the action with that line as its help, as refused() does for scene actions

## Expected impact
The learner sees the door is closed before pressing it. Could break: menu focus order if the action is removed rather than disabled.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the menu offers only what the check takes
Before: menu actions offered and then refused while a check is part way: 1 (my-topics)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - out of this round's paths (view.ts is linga's); the rows test above is S
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:754 `act("my-topics", "My topics", ..., { ...cmd(l.plan ? "plan-open" : "plan-propose"), ui: close })`
desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:364 the new refusal
instrument: a lingaView rows case in tools/linga-rules-test.cjs (linga context): with a part-way check open, the menu's my-topics action is disabled with a help line (or absent), and every offered action is one checkAccepts would take
